question: At which of the following sites of the Indus Valley Civilization was The Great Bath discovered?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohenjo-daro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Great Bath was discovered at Mohenjo-daro, one of the most important urban settlements of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• It is considered one of the earliest public water tanks in the ancient world, reflecting the advanced urban planning and sophisticated hydraulic engineering of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• The Great Bath is made from finely fitted bricks and is waterproofed with a layer of bitumen, showcasing the advanced construction techniques of the time.
 
• This site was likely used for ritual bathing or religious ceremonies, indicating the social and religious practices of the people of the Indus Valley Civilization.
